title: Agentic Reasoning and Tool Integration for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces ARTIST, a framework that enables large language models to reason with and act upon external tools and environments via reinforcement learning, achieving state-of-the-art results on mathematical reasoning and multi-turn function calling benchmarks.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You can use a calculator or a computer to help with the calculations. This is similar to how agentic reasoning works. It enables large language models (LLMs) to interact with external tools and environments to improve their problem-solving abilities.

By integrating tools into the reasoning process, LLMs can overcome their limitations and achieve more accurate results.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
The ARTIST framework uses reinforcement learning to train LLMs to interact with external tools and environments. The model generates multiple reasoning rollouts, alternating between text-based reasoning and tool interactions. The tool outputs are incorporated back into the reasoning chain, enabling iterative refinement and adaptive strategy adjustment.

This process allows the model to learn effective tool-use behaviors and develop flexible, adaptive, and interpretable problem-solving strategies.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
The ARTIST framework has been evaluated on several benchmarks, including mathematical reasoning and multi-turn function calling tasks. The results show that ARTIST consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, with up to 22% absolute improvement over base models.

On the τ-bench benchmark, ARTIST more than doubles the accuracy of base and prompt-based models.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The ARTIST framework has significant implications for the development of more advanced and generalizable LLMs. By integrating tools into the reasoning process, LLMs can overcome their limitations and achieve more accurate results.

This can lead to breakthroughs in various applications, such as natural language processing, computer vision, and decision-making systems.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
The ARTIST framework introduces several key innovations, including the use of reinforcement learning to train LLMs to interact with external tools and environments. The framework also uses a loss masking strategy to focus optimization on the model's reasoning and decision-making.

Additionally, the framework employs a composite reward mechanism to provide fine-grained feedback for each rollout.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try out the ARTIST framework, you can use the provided code and datasets to train and evaluate your own LLMs. You can also experiment with different tools and environments to see how they impact the reasoning process.

By exploring the possibilities of agentic reasoning, you can develop more advanced and generalizable LLMs that can tackle complex problems in various domains.
